still_true: Wegovy's US list price is still $1,349 a month, and almost nobody pays it.
The FDA has approved no generic semaglutide or tirzepatide in the US. Generic liraglutide is still the only generic incretin on the US market.
The TrumpRx cash channel still operates, and the oral Wegovy starting dose still costs $149 a month there.
The Medicare GLP-1 Bridge pilot has not been revived, Congress has not reopened the ~$41B CBO-scored permanent benefit, and Medicare still pays for no incretin prescribed for weight loss alone.

The September 2027 tri-agency guidance allowing up to 30% premium differentials tied to verified adherence still stands. Illinois's ban on adherence-conditioned premiums is still the only state ban in force, and the suicidal-ideation warning is still off the labels.

population.note:
FICTIONAL.

Cycling: 41.8% ever-used − 31.0% current = 10.8% of adults who used and are off now. About 54% of current users are on a second or later course (16.7 points), and 3.0 points have cycled and are off again, so (16.7 + 3.0) / 41.8 ≈ 47.1% of ever-users have cycled. The other 7.8 points stopped once and have not restarted.

Two-year flows (points of adults): 7.2 new starters, ~9.0 stops, ~8.1 restarts. Check: 24.7 + 7.2 + 8.1 − 9.0 = 31.0, and the off pool goes 9.9 + 9.0 − 8.1 = 10.8. Stopping is lower than in the parent because three groups are sticky: Medicare dementia-route users, those on $149–299 cash pills, and the remaining conditioned tracks. One-year persistence for new starters on weekly and oral products is still about one-third.

Age check: 0.20×18 + 0.33×31 + 0.24×42 + 0.23×31 = 3.6 + 10.23 + 10.08 + 7.13 ≈ 31.0. Income thirds average 31.0. The bottom third rose 8.5 points, from the $149 cash floor, Medicaid AUD growth and the Medicare dementia route. The top third rose only 4, because the 'unmedicated' ideal pulls some upper-income users off and they cycle off.

Users: 31.0% × ~277M adults ≈ 85.9M. FICTIONAL payer mix:
- Commercial ~14.2M (16.5%): ~6.9M on diabetes/CV/OSA/CKD codes, ~6.3M in conditioned weight tracks, ~1.0M on unconditional weight coverage.
- Medicare ~18.6M (21.7%): ~17.1M aged 65+ and ~1.5M under-65 disabled.
- Medicaid ~5.4M (6.3%): ~1.2M on the AUD label; ~0.7M in the five waiver states under adherence conditions.
- Legitimate cash ~42.7M (49.7%): ~7.5M on the indefinite $149 starting dose, ~3.6M on calm/focus plans, and ~3M who lost employer coverage in 2035–36 and moved to cash.
- Imported or counterfeit ~5.0M (5.8%).
Sum: 14.2 + 18.6 + 5.4 + 42.7 + 5.0 = 85.9. On-label AUD users ≈ 4.3M: 1.6M via calm platforms, 1.2M Medicaid, 1.0M Medicare, 0.5M commercial/EAP.

Adult obesity is ~31.0%. About 16% of adults have obesity and have never used a drug, concentrated in the rural South, uninsured 50–64s and adults 65+ who fail DXA or PA screens.

Pediatric, restated on an all-under-18 denominator of ~73M: ~4.6% of 12–17s (1.15M) and ~1.1% of 6–11s (0.26M, of whom ~35k are on tirzepatide after the Apr 2036 approval) ≈ 1.41M ≈ 1.9%. About 62% of 6–11 users are Medicaid/CHIP. About 6.1M children live with a parent who has regained after stopping. About 1.2M children have a parent in a Medicaid waiver state where the parent's coverage is conditioned and the child's, under EPSDT, is not.

access.public_coverage: Medicare (~18.6M users) still pays only through diabetes, CV, CKD, OSA, AUD and dementia-risk codes, behind prior authorisation. Since Oct 2035 the dementia-risk code includes adults 60+ with obesity and no CVD (tirzepatide). The Medicare-eligible part of that group drove most of the growth. FICTIONAL arithmetic: 18.6M × ~$205 average net/month × 12 ≈ $45.8B gross Part D incretin spend, up from $38.3B. Average net fell from $228 through deeper PBM rebates and lower TrumpRx-anchored net prices. Dementia route: ~4.6M × $215 × 12 ≈ $11.9B. AUD route: ~1.0M × $190 × 12 ≈ $2.3B. Bimagrumab, on its high-fracture-risk label only: ~0.4M × $580 × 12 ≈ $2.8B. The DXA national coverage decision pays for a scan every 24 months, ~9M scans a year × ~$80 ≈ $0.7B. Medicaid (~5.4M): AUD remains a covered outpatient use everywhere. 7 states still cover adult weight loss. Under Section 1115 waivers approved Sep 2035, Georgia, Tennessee, Arkansas, Oklahoma and Indiana condition adult incretin coverage, AUD included, on smart-bottle or pharmacy-verified adherence. ~90k adults were suspended for log gaps in the first six months. Children 6–11 and 12–17 stay covered under EPSDT, which the waivers do not touch.
access.generic_rest_of_world: Indian generic semaglutide still sells for $4–30 a month inside India and in 100+ export markets. Chinese tirzepatide-analogue vials still sell for $20–60 where patents are not enforced. The Section 232 tariff and Indian export-licence checks remain, so delivered US prices are ~$90–170, now barely below the $149 TrumpRx pill. Canadian and Brazilian generics have drifted down to CAD 40–70 and BRL 140–250. India and China still supply about two-thirds of world volume.
access.note:
FICTIONAL. Managed decline through negotiated channels, with no list cuts:
- TrumpRx: Wegovy pill starting dose $149 (unchanged); maintenance cut to $179 from $199; oral amycretin added Mar 2035 at $299, down from $449 direct.
- Foundayo $149–199. Injectable Wegovy/Zepbound $199–249. MariTide $229. Retatrutide $349.
- Lilly's tirzepatide + bimagrumab co-pack (Zepbound Strata, Feb 2036): $649 direct cash, the high end of the market. ~1.1M bimagrumab users by Dec 2036, ~0.4M of them on Medicare.

Employers: Business Group on Health puts coverage at 33% (2034), 28% (Nov 2035) and 24% (Nov 2036). About 80% of the employers still covering impose adherence and/or 5%-at-six-months conditions, and unconditional coverage is ~5% of employers. The stated reason is the cash floor: if a pill costs $149–299 at TrumpRx, coverage looks optional. About 2,000 mid-size employers replaced coverage with a taxable $75–125 'metabolic allowance' paid on proof of adherence from a pharmacy or smart bottle (~1.8M workers, counted as cash users). Coverage now concentrates on diabetes and cardiac codes, a hardened two-tier system. Orals are ~60% of users. The gray market shrank to ~5.0M because branded cash undercuts delivered imports. Domestic re-filling persists in the South.

drugs.pipeline_note:
FICTIONAL. Pipeline rules:
- Tirzepatide dementia extension (60+ without CVD): resubmitted Mar 2035, a class 2 resubmission, approved Oct 2035 with fracture language added after the women-70+ excess.
- Muscle-preserving combination (realises next_gen_launch): no new molecule was possible in-window. The driver is realised with an existing product in a new form. Lilly filed a bimagrumab sBLA and a co-pack with tirzepatide in Jan 2035, and FDA approved it Feb 2036, 13 months later.
- BELIEVE-2 trial (72 weeks): ~22% weight loss. Lean mass was ~8% of weight lost vs ~33% on tirzepatide alone, and total-hip BMD loss was roughly halved. There was no fracture endpoint, so a fracture-outcomes postmarketing trial is required, reading out no earlier than 2039.
- Tirzepatide 6–11 (SURMOUNT-Kids): filed Mar 2035, approved Apr 2036. Height velocity was ~0.6 cm/year below expected at 72 weeks.
- Implants are still in phase 2 and not on the market. No oral matches retatrutide's ~24%.
- Novo has no activin antibody. It filed CagriSema with a resistance-training software device bundle, which FDA declined to review as a combination product.
- Global incretin market ~$225B (2035). US branded net prices keep drifting down 3–5% a year, and TrumpRx cash prices stepped down as stated in access.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of discontinuation outside clinic tracks. Starting-dose long-term users report less of it, which partly explains why they stay.

safety_ledger.effect: Gastroparesis, ileus and bowel obstruction (persistent delayed gastric emptying)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: The first federal MDL gastroparesis bellwether (Jun 2035) ended in a defence verdict on causation. The second (Nov 2035) hung. GI claims sit at ~41,000, and persistence after stopping is still disputed.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: No new labelling. More bellwethers are scheduled for 2036–37.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Elevated with rapid weight loss; unchanged.
No causal confirmation; absolute risk low. Still pleaded alongside EPI.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; folded into the EPI mass tort.

safety_ledger.effect: Lean mass (muscle) loss and bone-density loss
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Now treated as a population problem; see the hip-fracture entry. DXA studies find lean mass is ~25–40% of weight lost on monotherapy, more in users 65+ and in cyclers who regain mostly fat. Medicare hip-fracture HR is ~1.3 after more than 2 years of use and ~1.45 after three or more cycles.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class Warnings and Precautions upgraded Oct 2035, with baseline DXA advised for adults 65+ and postmenopausal women 50+ and resistance-exercise counselling. No boxed warning. CMS covers DXA every 24 months on-drug. Bimagrumab label broadened Feb 2036.

safety_ledger.effect: Population hip-fracture, fall and frailty burden in older and long-term users
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: A FDA–CMS Sentinel analysis (Jun 2035) of ~9.6M Medicare beneficiaries with more than 2 years of use estimated ~13,000 excess hip fractures a year: baseline ~4.5/1,000 × 9.6M ≈ 43,000, × HR 0.3 ≈ 13,000. With ~20% one-year mortality after hip fracture, that implies ~2,600 attributable deaths a year. The excess is concentrated in women 70+, the starting-dose long-term group and users with EPI malabsorption. Orthopaedic wards and rehab facilities in Florida and Arizona report it as a caseload shift.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Same class warning upgrade. The dementia-route label requires baseline DXA for women 70+. USPSTF began an evidence review of osteoporosis screening in incretin users. Medicare Advantage plans added strength-class benefits.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Conflicting cohorts; absolute risk very low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Listed in adverse reactions; no class warning.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No new adult signal, including in AUD-label and dementia-route users. The pediatric psychiatric signal remains restrictive eating.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: The 2033 FDA study's ~7% vs ~3.5% (maintenance dose) and ~10% on retatrutide still stand. An NIH-funded low-dose study (QUIET-LD, ~6,000 calm-plan and starting-dose users) enrolled in 2035 and reads out in 2037. Prevalence at low doses is still unmeasured.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: No labelling change. FDA sent a warning letter, its first, to one calm platform over 'appetite-preserving' claims; untitled letters to others.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Half to two-thirds regain within 18 months, worse after repeated cycles. Regain after cycling is disproportionately fat, which compounds the lean-mass problem. ~90k Medicaid waiver suspensions produced abrupt stops.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None directly; it still underpins conditioned coverage and the waivers.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: B12, iron, vitamin D and thiamine deficiency (AUD users who keep drinking). Low ferritin in adolescent girls. Low protein intake is now recognised as a driver of lean loss in starting-dose cash users who have no dietitian.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Annual micronutrient panel language; protein-intake counselling added in the Oct 2035 class update.

safety_ledger.effect: Exocrine pancreatic insufficiency after 5+ years of continuous use
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: ~2× EPI incidence after more than 5 years of semaglutide; tirzepatide HR ~1.3. EPI claims ~58,000. The DOJ civil investigative demand into Novo is unresolved, and the first EPI bellwether is set for late 2036 and has not been tried.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: EPI wording on semaglutide and tirzepatide labels. The FDA Form 483 follow-up inspection closed with voluntary action indicated.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~5 years; effects in children on drug for decades; effects of repeated on/off cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About fourteen years of semaglutide follow-up now exist. Cycling effects on bone are clearer, and on pancreas still unclear. There are no data on indefinite starting-dose use or on bimagrumab beyond ~3 years.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Pediatric growth and bone PMRs extended to tirzepatide 6–11. Bimagrumab fracture-outcomes PMR.

safety_ledger.effect: Compounded / counterfeit / imported product harms (dosing errors, contamination, substitution)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Adverse-event reports tied to non-approved product passed ~36,000. Domestic re-filling from smuggled API persists in Mississippi, Alabama and Louisiana, with a second, smaller Burkholderia cluster in 2035 (~60 cases, 1 death). Bimagrumab knock-offs ('activin blockers') appear in gym gray channels.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Tariff and export checks unchanged. FDA import alert on unapproved activin-antibody products (2036). No statute or state action.

safety_ledger.effect: Growth deceleration, delayed puberty and restrictive eating in children started young
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Liraglutide and semaglutide 6–11 PMR data show a ~0.5–0.6 cm/year height-velocity deficit, partly reversible after stopping. SURMOUNT-Kids (tirzepatide) showed ~0.6 cm/year. The Swedish ARFID HR is ~1.8. Final adult height is still unknown. The earliest liraglutide 6–11 starters are now ~13–14.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Tirzepatide 6–11 approved with the same monitoring language and medication guide, no REMS. AAP still prefers lifestyle-first for prepubertal children.

safety_ledger.effect: Alcohol-related harms on the AUD label (dehydration, alcoholic ketoacidosis, aspiration with vomiting during binge drinking)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: The rate holds at ~1 per 2,000 person-years during titration. Abrupt stops after Medicaid waiver suspensions are linked in Georgia case reports to rebound drinking.

safety_ledger.effect: Bimagrumab adjunct effects (muscle spasms, diarrhoea, acne, possible lipid and hepatic changes)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: In BELIEVE-2, muscle spasms affected ~30% early on and led ~6% to discontinue. Mild ALT elevations occurred. Off-label use by under-50s without an incretin is uncharacterised.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; hepatic monitoring language; fracture-outcomes PMR.

food_and_beverage.state: About 47% of US households now have a user. Snack and confectionery volumes are down ~15–17% from 2025, sugary drinks ~13%, and dollar sales fell for a second year. The industry splits by zip code. In mass and value zips, small-pack and protein-fortified 'on-plan' lines are the standard SKU. In the top tier, the 'appetite' premium grows: aged butter, whole-milk dairy, heritage bakery and 'proudly full-fat' brands gain share in Austin, Brooklyn and Marin and are marketed as food for people who are not on anything. Protein supplements and creatine boom on the DXA advice.

alcohol.state: US spirits volumes are down ~21% from 2025 and beer ~14%. The AUD label now reaches ~4.3M people, many of them in the heavy-drinking core. Kentucky bourbon has shed ~3,000 jobs since 2033, and two Bardstown-area distilleries mothballed stills. Craft brewers in Ohio and Michigan consolidate. 'Calm-compatible' non-alcoholic lines pass 6% of category dollars. Natural wine and mezcal hold up in upper-income zips as part of the unmedicated aesthetic.

restaurants.state: Traffic is flat nationally and the business has split. Casual dining runs portion tiers and protein-forward 'track menus'. Bar and late-night revenue keeps falling in Dayton, Toledo and Columbus. In Austin and Brooklyn, 'appetite rooms' (long tasting menus, family-style feasts, bread courses) sell out to diners who treat eating a lot as a display. QSR value menus hold in Memphis-type markets.

apparel.state: Plus-size specialists keep shrinking. Mass retailers stock the 'slow-thin' middle and stretch for cyclers. Fashion's top tier moved to fuller, muscled fits, broad shoulders and thick thighs, and away from the gaunt 2030 silhouette, which now reads as cheap. Structured athletic wear and tailoring for gained muscle keep growing.

fitness.state: Growing fastest of any adjacent sector. Label counselling, DXA results and Zepbound Strata's marketing all point to resistance training. Medicare Advantage plans added strength benefits, and senior strength studios spread through Florida and Arizona suburbs. Budget chains run InBody and DXA partnerships. Upper-income 'unmedicated' gyms in Austin sell assay-verified memberships.

insurance.state: Employers retreat: weight-management coverage fell from 33% to 24% of employers, and those that remain mostly condition it. Coverage concentrates on diabetes and cardiac codes, and ~2,000 firms moved to adherence-conditioned cash allowances. Commercial pharmacy trend is ~+5% because PA denial rates rose. Part D gross incretin spend is ~$45.8B, the dementia route is the fastest-growing line, and Part D premiums rose again for 2036. CMS's AUD coding audit found ~11% of telehealth-originated AUD claims unsupported and recouped from two platforms. Medicaid waiver states report small savings and new administrative costs.

pharma.state: Growing without a shock. Lilly gains most from the dementia extension, Zepbound Strata and pediatric tirzepatide. Novo's oral amycretin, now on TrumpRx at $299, is the volume leader, while it carries a ~$6.2B reserve and the DOJ inquiry. Amgen's MariTide holds the clinic tracks as they shrink. Smart-bottle and adherence-verification vendors grow with the Medicaid waivers and allowances. Indian exporters keep redirecting volume to Gulf, Latin American and African markets.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Thin no longer signals much. The $149 pill made it common, and in Memphis or Tulsa slow-thin reads as cash and starting dose. Muscle on a thin frame reads as Strata or a trainer, which costs money. The scarce body is fuller, strong, visibly fed and provably off drug. A dried-blood-spot assay (Clearline, $89) now settles the question on dating apps and in some Austin gyms. For people over 65 the body signals something else: the DXA T-score has become a dinner-table number, and a walker after a hip fracture is now read as a drug story.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: The class line inverted at the top and hardened below. Upper-income 30–45s in Austin, Brooklyn and Charlotte treat 'unmedicated' as the boast, and some stop or hide use, cycling off before an assay. Others buy Strata to get the muscled look while still medicated. Thinness moved down-market: the bottom third's use rose fastest, and Medicaid children make up ~62% of 6–11 users. MAHA influencers adopted 'unmedicated vitality' as their own aesthetic, which put the anti-drug wing of the backlash on the same side as luxury food brands.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Two tables. In the medicated majority, meals are short, protein-first and logged. In the upper tier, the long meal came back as performance: second helpings, bread courses and 'feast nights' posted with assay badges. Bread Alone, at ~1,300 congregations, gained members, and its suppers attract appetite-curious professionals alongside its religious core, to some friction. School-lunch fights moved to whether nurses may record tirzepatide doses for 6–11s, and to protein standards.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Apps carry three tags: 'calm plan', 'on AUD treatment' and, since Nov 2035, a lab-verified 'unmedicated' badge, which ~4% of users in New York and Austin display. Matches with the badge get about twice the replies in those cities. Critics call it a purity test; users call it disclosure. Hiding use from a partner, known as 'stealth dosing', is a new couples-therapy presentation.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Appetite has become a status good. For the medicated majority it is still noise a subscription manages. For the top tier, having one, and showing it, is the scarce thing. Calm platforms responded by selling low doses as 'quiet the bottle, keep the table', promising craving loss without appetite loss, a claim FDA called unsupported. In the Delta the tariff is still 'the hunger tax'. In Georgia and Tennessee the waiver suspensions are called 'the log tax'.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Maintenance-dose anhedonia is still ~7% vs ~3.5% in controls, and ~10% on retatrutide. Calm/focus plans grew from 2.4M to ~3.6M subscribers, mostly on the Wegovy pill at $149–179 or Foundayo, plus a $39–59 fee. ~45% are written on the AUD label, and platforms add a 'focus' tier sold to knowledge workers. QUIET-LD will report the low-dose rate in 2037; until then it is unmeasured.
interior_life.framing: Platforms: 'quiet the noise', 'quiet the bottle, keep the table'. Manufacturers: 'food noise', 'reduced heavy drinking days'. HR and allowance vendors: steadiness and 'metabolic consistency'. Clinicians: dose-related blunting. Unmuted and the unmedicated-vitality crowd: 'a sedative for the people who can't afford to be interesting'.
interior_life.effect_on_work: Conditioned commercial tracks shrank to ~6.3M as employers dropped coverage, but conditioning spread sideways. ~1.8M workers get a $75–125 monthly allowance only while their smart bottle or pharmacy confirms fills. EAPs at trucking, warehousing and call centres still dispense the AUD pill. FMCSA still says nothing about calm plans. Benefit brokers still buy de-identified 'focus' cohorts. The two EEOC charges remain unresolved, and the EEOC has issued no guidance on allowances.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: 'Off' memoir gave way to 'appetite' memoir and feast cinema. 'Dry' stand-up continues, now mocking assay badges. Live-music venues in Columbus and Louisville keep cutting nights, while Austin supper-club music rooms grow. Sportsbook handle per account keeps falling in insured suburbs. Ambient streaming 'calm' tiers bundle with platforms.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Pill windows and shot days still structure mornings. New presentations: the hidden-use partner; the sober-on-pill partner and the drinking partner; and, in the 65+ group, couples rearranging homes after one partner's DXA result. Libido complaints split by dose, and calm-plan users report less of the 'absence' that full-dose partners describe.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: The 2036 presidential campaign argues over three numbers: the ~$12B dementia route in Part D, ~13,000 excess hip fractures and ~90k Medicaid waiver suspensions. Nobody proposes repealing the Medicare weight-loss exclusion. The Let Them Grow coalition, now opposed to pediatric tirzepatide, splits: its MAHA wing embraced 'unmedicated vitality', while Unmuted focuses on calm platforms and the waivers. 'Sedated electorate' claims still lack turnout evidence.

state.regulatory_posture: Federal, routine and permissive on approvals: dementia extension, Strata and pediatric tirzepatide. Firmer on safety communication: a class fracture warning, the first warning letter to a calm platform, an import alert on activin knock-offs. Punitive on imports, with the Section 232 tariff unchanged. No state passed a statute, and Illinois remains the only ban.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: No new subsidy, and Congress has not acted on the permanent benefit. The CMS DXA national coverage decision is the only new federal payment line. TrumpRx price steps were negotiated, not legislated. OPM's FEHB adherence and progress conditions continue for plan years 2035–36. The 2027 30% premium-differential guidance stands.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Benefits conditioning is now public policy as well as employer practice. Section 1115 waivers (Sep 2035) in Georgia, Tennessee, Arkansas, Oklahoma and Indiana tie adult Medicaid incretin coverage, AUD included, to smart-bottle or pharmacy-verified adherence. A National Health Law Program suit in D.D.C. argues the waivers exceed 1115 authority, and no ruling has issued. Texas ERS and Georgia's state health benefit plan condition state-employee coverage the same way. Employer allowances run on the same fill feeds. CMS's AUD audit pulled telehealth AUDIT-C records from four platforms.
state.workforce_or_military: TRICARE covers AUD and dementia-route use under existing rules. The Army recruit oral pilot is unchanged. DoD added DXA to the separation physical for long-term incretin users after the fracture analysis. FMCSA still covers only on-label AUD use.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: The 100% Section 232 tariff and India's export-licence checks remain. Beijing's WTO complaint reached panel stage without a ruling. Branded US and Danish plants supply the TrumpRx channel. Bimagrumab is made in Lilly's US biologics plants. Indian and Chinese generics dominate Gulf, African and Latin American markets, and in Mexico and Brazil generic semaglutide sells for less than US snack-food budgets.

events.event: TrumpRx adds Novo's oral amycretin at $299 a month and cuts Wegovy pill maintenance to $179; Lilly and Novo set direct injectable prices at $199–249. Within weeks several large self-insured employers say they will drop weight-management coverage for 2036, and by November the share of employers covering it falls to 28%

CMS approves Section 1115 waivers letting Georgia, Tennessee, Arkansas, Oklahoma and Indiana condition adult Medicaid incretin coverage, alcohol-use-disorder prescriptions included, on smart-bottle-verified adherence; children stay exempt under EPSDT, and ~90,000 adults are suspended for log gaps within six months

FDA extends tirzepatide's dementia-risk label to adults 60+ with obesity and no heart disease. The same action upgrades class-wide fracture and sarcopenia warnings after a June FDA–CMS Sentinel analysis estimated ~13,000 excess hip fractures a year among long-term Medicare users. CMS will now pay for a bone-density scan every two years

A major dating app adds a lab-verified 'unmedicated' badge backed by Clearline's $89 dried-blood-spot incretin assay; badged profiles get about twice the replies in New York and Austin, and two Austin gyms begin requiring the test for 'natural' memberships

FDA approves Lilly's Zepbound Strata, tirzepatide co-packaged with monthly subcutaneous bimagrumab, for adults 50+ or with documented lean-mass loss (filed Jan 2035); the launch campaign 'Lose the weight. Keep the body.' runs at $649 a month cash, though the trial had no fracture endpoint

FDA approves weekly tirzepatide for children 6–11 with obesity (filed Mar 2035), with the same growth-monitoring language as semaglutide and a height-velocity deficit of ~0.6 cm a year in its trial; most early prescriptions are written in Medicaid clinics

open_tensions: Bones against brains. The dementia extension put ~4.6M Medicare users, many of them women 70+, on a drug with a labelled fracture excess. Strata is sold as the fix on lean-mass and BMD surrogates, with no fracture data before ~2039. Medicare pays for it only on the narrow high-risk label.

Two tiers with logs on both. Employers retreated to a cash floor of $149–299, while 7.5M people stay indefinitely on an unstudied starting dose. Medicaid adults in five states lose coverage over smart-bottle gaps, while their children, on two approved 6–11 drugs, are covered unconditionally. The NHeLP suit is undecided.

Thinness is now cheap and the unmedicated body is the luxury. That pushes upper-income users toward hidden use and assays and pushes the drug down-market, into the bottom third and Medicaid pediatrics, where growth deficits and fracture risk will show up first.

Calm platforms grew to 3.6M by selling low-dose blunting with an AUD code attached. CMS recouped unsupported claims, FDA sent its first warning letter, and QUIET-LD's 2037 readout will either legitimise or puncture the whole category.

prose.headline: Thin Is Cheap Now: 86 million Americans on the pill, and the rich want to prove they're not
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2036 nearly one American adult in three takes an incretin drug, about eighty-six million people. More than four in ten have tried one. The growth came from the bottom, not the top, and that is the strangest fact about the country now.

The price did most of the work, through negotiation rather than collapse. In March 2035 the federal cash channel added Novo's oral amycretin at $299 a month and cut the Wegovy pill's maintenance dose to $179. The starting pill stayed at $149, and about seven and a half million people now take it indefinitely because it is what they can afford, a regimen no one has studied. List prices did not move, and there is still no American generic. But once a pill that works can be had for the price of a phone plan, employers stopped paying for one. Coverage for weight loss fell from a third of employers to under a quarter. Most of those still paying want proof: a smart bottle that reports when it is opened, a scan, five percent of body weight gone in six months. A couple of thousand firms dropped coverage altogether and pay a taxable monthly allowance instead, released when the pharmacy feed confirms a fill. Insurance now follows diagnosis codes, diabetes and heart disease and dementia risk. Everyone else pays cash, and half of all users do.

The states joined in. In September 2035 Washington let Georgia, Tennessee, Arkansas, Oklahoma and Indiana condition Medicaid coverage of the drugs on logged adherence, alcohol prescriptions included. Ninety thousand adults were suspended in six months for gaps in their logs. Their children were not, because federal rules for children's medical necessity cover them regardless. By April there were two drugs approved for six-to-eleven-year-olds, after tirzepatide joined semaglutide. Both slow growth by about half a centimetre a year, and both are written mostly in Medicaid clinics.

Older Americans arrived through a different door. In October 2035 tirzepatide's dementia label was widened to anyone over sixty with obesity, heart disease or not. Medicare, which still pays nothing for weight alone, now spends about twelve billion dollars a year on that one route. The same regulatory action carried the bill. A federal analysis had estimated thirteen thousand extra hip fractures a year among long-term Medicare users, most of them women over seventy, and the class warning was strengthened. Medicare began paying for a bone scan every two years, and the T-score became something people mention at dinner. In February Lilly launched Zepbound Strata, tirzepatide packaged with a muscle-preserving antibody, under the line Lose the weight, keep the body. It costs $649 a month in cash. The trial measured muscle and bone density but not fractures.

As thinness got cheap, it stopped meaning much. In Austin and Brooklyn the boast now is an appetite: long dinners, bread courses, full-fat butter, thick thighs in the fashion pages. A dating app sells a lab-verified unmedicated badge backed by an $89 blood-spot test, and the badge roughly doubles replies. Some people stop before the test, and some hide their pills from partners. The parents' movement that rallied against pediatric approvals took up unmedicated vitality as its look, which leaves it on the same side as the luxury dairy brands.

The calm platforms grew to three and a half million subscribers. They sell low doses for quiet, and nearly half of them are now written up as alcohol treatment. Federal auditors found one claim in nine unsupported. A study that will finally measure what low doses do to pleasure reports next year. Bourbon is down a fifth. The country is quieter, thinner, logged, and a little more breakable.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Tanya Rhodes wakes at 5:10 in Macon and takes the pill before her feet touch the floor, because the bottle on the nightstand counts. The bottle blinks green and the Peach State Medicaid app shows a streak of 212 days. Her cousin Lorraine missed four days in February when her phone died, and they suspended her. Lorraine started drinking again by April.

Tanya's pill is written for alcohol, and the code is true. She has not wanted a drink since last spring. Mostly she does not want much of anything before noon. She waters it down in her own head and calls it peace.

DeShawn is nine, and his shot is Thursday. On the fridge is the growth chart from the pediatric clinic, with its dotted line he keeps falling under by a little. Nobody at the clinic asks about her bottle, and nobody at her program asks about his chart.

At the warehouse the break room television plays an ad for Strata: a silver-haired woman deadlifting, and the line Lose the weight. Keep the body. Her supervisor, a thin guy from Atlanta, says his wife pays cash for it. He says six forty-nine like it's a car payment.

At lunch Tanya eats half a chicken thigh and saves the rest for DeShawn.

At night her sister texts a screenshot from a dating app showing a man with a little gold badge: UNMEDICATED. VERIFIED. Look at him, her sister writes, eating a whole pie on purpose.

Tanya looks for a while. Then she sets the bottle back where it can see her.
